description: Defects planted into a staged copy of the fixture, each an exact-string edit. Every one changes a constant that encode and decode, or conversion and its inverse, share, so the mutant is internally consistent and a suite that only round-trips cannot see it. Only a test that knows the protocol's own value can.

defects.title: The checksum's position weights use the wrong offset
defects.rationale: Encode and decode share one checksum function, so every frame still round-trips. Only a frame whose checksum byte is known from the protocol exposes it.

defects.title: The checksum's final XOR mask is wrong
defects.rationale: Shared by encode and decode, so round trips pass. Visible only against a known checksum byte.

defects.title: Node and sequence are written in the wrong order
defects.rationale: Applied identically on both sides, so a frame survives encode then decode. Only the byte layout the protocol fixes tells them apart.

defects.title: An odd-length payload is padded with the wrong byte
defects.rationale: Decode ignores the pad, and the checksum is computed over whatever was written, so everything stays self-consistent.

defects.title: The depth unit's length is wrong
defects.rationale: to_metres and from_metres share the constant, so converting there and back returns what went in. A known conversion exposes it.

defects.title: The sequence counter wraps at the wrong value
defects.rationale: Every ordinary run of sequence numbers behaves the same. It shows only at and after the top of the range.
